title: The Lord's Animals
summary: When the Creator fashioned all the animals of the earth, he created gentle sheep, strong horses, noble hounds, and industrious bees to bless and assist humankind in their daily lab...
full_text:
When the Creator fashioned all the animals of the earth, he created gentle sheep, strong horses, noble hounds, and industrious bees to bless and assist humankind in their daily labors.

An envious spirit, looking upon this peaceful harmony with spite, resolved to create creatures of his own. He formed the fierce wolf to devour the sheep, the stinging hornet to torment the horses, and the thorny thistle to choke the grain fields.

The Creator looked upon these wild creations with boundless wisdom. Rather than destroying them, he brought them into cosmic harmony: he gave the sheep a loyal shepherd and protective hounds to guard against the wolf; he gave the birds appetite to eat the hornets; and he decreed that the donkey should find sweet nourishment in the prickly thistles.

Thus, even creatures formed in malice were integrated into the grand tapestry of nature, showing that wisdom transforms all things into a higher order of balance and purpose.
moral: Every creature has its appointed place in the balance of creation, serving harmony.

quiz.question: What is the central moral lesson taught in "The Lord's Animals"?
options: Presence of mind and quiet wisdom triumph over brute strength.
Acting in haste and anger without thinking
Believing rumors and flattery without proof
quiz.hint: Remember the moral lesson of this traditional story.

quiz.question: How do the characters overcome their challenge?
options: Through patience, calm reflection, and wisdom
By shouting loudly and blaming others
By running away from every problem
quiz.hint: Consider the virtues praised in world folklore.

quiz.question: What memorable conclusion does this story teach young readers?
options: Honesty, kindness, and clear thinking lead to peace
quiz.hint: Reflect upon the resolution of the story.
